st: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Season the chicken with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Mix the grated yam and taro with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and half the coconut cream to form a thick, damp paste.
Soften the banana leaves over a flame or in hot water, then lay two overlapping leaves in a baking dish.
Spread half the root paste on the leaves, add the chicken, then cover with the remaining paste.
Pour the rest of the coconut cream over the top.
Fold the leaves over to seal and cover the dish tightly with foil.
Bake for [[90 minutes]] until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and the pudding is firm.
Rest 10 minutes, then slice into squares.
Peel the cassava and grate it finely, then squeeze it in a cloth to remove extra liquid.
Mix with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and a few spoonfuls of the coconut cream.
Blanch the greens in boiling water for 1 minute and drain.
Lay out 2 or 3 leaves and put a spoonful of cassava mixture on them.
Roll up like a cigar, tucking in the sides.
Place the rolls in a pot with a banana leaf on the bottom.
Pour [[0.5 cup]] coconut cream over the rolls and add water to come half way up.
Cover and simmer gently for [[40 minutes]] until the cassava is cooked through.
Serve hot with the cooking liquid.
Grate the cassava finely and squeeze in a cloth to remove extra liquid.
Mix with [[0.5 cup]] grated coconut and [[1 tsp]] salt to make a thick dough.
Season the pork with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Soften banana leaves over a flame, then lay one flat.
Press a flat layer of dough in the center of the leaf.
Add a spoonful of pork, then cover with more dough, forming a ball.
Fold the leaf tightly around the parcel and tie with string.
Steam covered for [[90 minutes]], keeping water in the pot, until the pork reaches 145°F (63°C) or more.
Cool for 10 minutes before unwrapping.
Put the taro, plantains and breadfruit in a large pot with [[6 cups]] water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Bring to a boil.
Cook for [[30 minutes]] until all of them are very soft.
Drain well, saving some of the liquid.
Pound or mash the roots in a large bowl until smooth and stretchy.
Add a splash of cooking liquid if it is too stiff.
Spoon into bowls and make a well in the center of each.
Pour [[1 cup]] coconut cream around the roots and serve warm.
Put [[0.5 cup]] ground kava in a clean muslin cloth or fine strainer bag.
Place it in a large bowl.
Pour in [[1 cup]] cool water.
Knead and squeeze the bag in the water for 5 minutes, until it turns a muddy brown.
Add [[1 cup]] more water, then knead 5 minutes.
Repeat with the last [[1 cup]] water.
Wring out the bag very well and discard the pulp.
Serve at once in small cups. It numbs the mouth slightly and should be sipped slowly.
